dedupe_keys.name: micro econometric model of digital television adoption and analogue switch off policy calibrated to uk data adda and ottaviani 2004

description: This 2004 working paper studies how economic policy shapes the transition from analogue to digital television, focusing on switching off the analogue terrestrial signal. The analogue signal cannot credibly be switched off until almost all viewers have migrated, yet before switch-off only part of the population can be reached by digital and viewers pay more for equipment. After reviewing market structure, government intervention and the early experience of industrialised countries, the authors formulate a micro-econometric model of digital television adoption by individual viewers, calibrate it to UK data, and simulate government policies. Take-up can be changed by controlling signal quality and public service content, subsidising equipment, and publicising switch-off conditions and dates; if switch-off is conditional on aggregate adoption, strategic delays can arise and expectations affect success. Producer: Jérôme Adda and Marco Ottaviani, September 2004, with ESRC support. Coverage: United Kingdom, with international experience reviewed. Access: free PDF; the abstract and opening were read. No code or data files are released on the page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence not stated. Caveats: calibrated to early-2000s UK data and not a released tool. Simulation uses: the adoption model is a template for household-level simulation of technology transitions in broadcasting. Related record: the ITU digital dividend report (data-itu-digital-dividend-insights-spectrum-decisions-2018).
